clue.text: Strike restricting a corporation

indicators.note: restricting means holding in, so the word for strike closes round the a

parts.note: to strike someone is to punch them

explanation.surface: A walkout that hampers a large company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Corporation' reads as a business, but it is an old jocular word for a large belly.
explanation.definitionFit: Corporation is a dated humorous term for a big stomach, the same as a pot belly.

clue.text: Friend with brilliant home — a big expensive one

parts.note: a pal is a friend
ace is informal for brilliant or excellent

explanation.surface: A friend with a splendid house, and a very costly one at that.
explanation.definitionFit: A grand, costly residence, such as a royal one, is called a palace.

clue.text: Nicer aunt sadly in a dither?

indicators.note: sadly suggests the letters of nicer aunt have gone wrong and must be rearranged

explanation.surface: A kinder relative who is unhappily flustered.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone in a dither is hesitant and undecided, unable to make up their mind.

clue.text: Flags? Officer comes with yours and mine

parts.note: Col is the abbreviation for colonel, a military officer
what belongs to you and me is ours

explanation.surface: A senior officer arrives bringing the possessions of both of us.
explanation.definitionFit: A regiment's or ship's colours are its flags or standards.

clue.text: Somehow happier having penned grand words at front of book?

indicators.note: having penned means enclosing, so the shuffled letters hold the abbreviation inside them
somehow hints that the letters of happier come out in some other order

parts.note: G is slang shorthand for a grand, a thousand pounds or dollars

explanation.surface: A cheerful writer has put some grand words at the start of a book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Somehow' rearranges HAPPIER into EPIRAPH, and 'having penned' puts G inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: An epigraph is a quotation set at the opening of a book or chapter.

clue.text: Folk making request? No respite, it could possibly appear

indicators.note: could possibly says the letters of no respite it might form something else when rearranged

explanation.surface: Pleaders get no rest from something that might turn up.
explanation.definitionFit: People who put a formal plea or appeal to an authority are those making a request.

clue.text: Place for car containing black stuff in bins?

indicators.note: containing means the word for a car's place holds the letter inside it

parts.note: a garage is where a car is kept
B is the standard abbreviation for black, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A car shelter holding dark rubbish waiting to be thrown out.
explanation.definitionFit: Rubbish thrown away into dustbins is garbage, the American word for refuse.

clue.text: A male needs employment, please

parts.note: employment of something is its use

explanation.surface: A man needs a job, he begs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Please' looks like a polite plea at the end, but it is the verb meaning to delight.
explanation.definitionFit: To please someone is to entertain or divert them, which is to keep them amused.

clue.text: Vindaloo for a remarkable person?

definitions.meaning: a vindaloo is a fiercely spicy curry, something fiery to eat
an impressive, exciting or highly capable individual is colloquially called this

explanation.definitionFit: A fiery curry is literally very spicy food, and the same phrase is slang for someone outstanding.

clue.text: See hundred drink in this place

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look or see
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred
ale is a drink, a kind of beer

explanation.surface: Look, a hundred drinks to be had in this spot.
explanation.definitionFit: A locale is a site or setting where something happens.

clue.text: Daughter with us in the beginning seen as magical

definitions.note: the adjective stands for the noun: a magical quality or glamour

indicators.note: in places the daughter-and-us letters within the word for the beginning

parts.note: the beginning of something is its start
taken as written

explanation.surface: A daughter with us at the start is regarded as enchanting.
explanation.definitionFit: Stardust is the dreamy, enchanting quality associated with romance or celebrity, a sprinkling of magic.

clue.text: Gosh — bet the French tucking in will get fat!

parts.note: cor is a British exclamation of surprise, like gosh

indicators.note: tucking in means the French article is tucked inside the word for a bet

parts.note: a punt is a bet or gamble
le is French for the

explanation.surface: Wow, eating French food will make you put on weight!
explanation.definitionFit: Corpulent is a formal word for overweight or stout.

clue.text: Our lad's role could be making money

indicators.note: could be signals that the letters of our lad's role might be arranged into something else

explanation.surface: Our boy's job might bring in cash.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in lad's is no letter, but its S is: OURLADSROLE is the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Eurodollars are US dollars held in banks outside America, a form of currency.

clue.text: Notice record time — it's very good

parts.note: an ad is a notice, an advertisement
an EP is an extended-play record

explanation.surface: An advertisement promotes a record that's said to be excellent.
explanation.definitionFit: Adept means highly skilled or proficient at something.

clue.text: A freeness lost? It becomes tricky to state opinions boldly

indicators.note: the letters of a freeness lost become tricky, twisted into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Lost freedom makes it hard to speak one's mind.
explanation.definitionFit: To speak up confidently and forcefully for one's views is to be assertive about them.

clue.text: Old lover with the action of a twister said to be taking too much money

parts.note: an ex is a former partner

indicators.note: said to be marks a word that sounds like the one written down

parts.note: twisting force is torsion

explanation.surface: A former partner, a crook, is accused of overcharging.
explanation.walkthrough: A twister is a swindler in the surface, but here it is whatever twists.
explanation.definitionFit: Extortion is obtaining money by force or threats, or charging far too much.

clue.text: Social reformer in church, one painting a picture maybe

parts.note: someone who paints a picture is an artist, for example

explanation.surface: A campaigner for change in a church, perhaps a painter at work.
explanation.definitionFit: The Chartists were a 19th-century British movement campaigning for votes and political reform.

clue.text: A ton? Hang on, we say, it's a lot less than a ton!

definitions.text: it's a lot less than a ton!

parts.note: a ton is slang for a hundred

indicators.note: we say indicates the word as spoken, matched with a different spelling

parts.note: hang on means wait

explanation.surface: Someone queries a weight, insisting it's far below a ton.
explanation.walkthrough: A hundredweight is an imperial unit, 112 pounds in Britain, so a twentieth of a ton.
explanation.definitionFit: A hundredweight is a twentieth of a ton, so far lighter than one.

clue.text: Regret about one responsible for coded messages

parts.note: re means about or concerning
Samuel Morse devised the dot-and-dash code for telegraph messages

explanation.surface: Sorrow over a codemaker's work.
explanation.definitionFit: Remorse is deep regret for a wrong one has done.

clue.text: Good American row — it's becoming stormier

parts.note: a tier is a row, as of seats

explanation.surface: A fine American quarrel is getting more heated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' reads as a quarrel; it is a line of seats.
explanation.definitionFit: Gustier weather has stronger blasts of wind, so it is wilder and windier.

clue.text: Two loveless mischief-makers shortly appearing in middle of the day?

indicators.note: love is zero, so loveless drops the round letter from two
shortly cuts the word for mischief-makers short by its final letter

parts.note: elves are mischievous little sprites

explanation.surface: A pair of heartless pranksters turn up briefly at noon.
explanation.definitionFit: Midday falls at twelve o'clock, so the number marks the middle of the day.

clue.text: Field left with a lot of paper around

indicators.note: around means the paper quantity wraps about the letter for left

parts.note: a ream is a large quantity of paper, 500 sheets

explanation.surface: A meadow abandoned with heaps of paper strewn about.
explanation.definitionFit: A realm is a field or sphere of activity or interest.

clue.text: Top character gets record with cry of surprise going round

indicators.note: going round means the exclamation encircles the record

parts.note: aha is an exclamation of surprise or discovery
an LP is a long-playing record

explanation.surface: A leading figure gets a record and people gasp.
explanation.definitionFit: Alpha is the first letter of the Greek alphabet, so it heads the list of characters.

clue.text: Breaker for ship of the desert?

definitions.text: Breaker for ship of the desert?

parts.words: Breaker for ship of the desert?
parts.note: the ship of the desert is the camel, and the proverb says one final straw broke its back

explanation.definitionFit: The final small burden that breaks the camel's back is the proverbial final straw.

clue.text: Sovereign put at risk has head of army brought in

indicators.note: brought in places that first letter inside the word for put at risk

parts.note: to imperil is to put at risk

indicators.note: head of means the first letter of army

explanation.surface: A monarch endangered by the army's commander being brought into play.
explanation.definitionFit: Imperial means relating to an emperor or empire, so supreme or royal in rank.

clue.text: First bit of icing in last bit of decoration

indicators.note: in puts that letter inside the word for last

parts.note: final means last

indicators.note: first bit of picks the opening letter of icing

explanation.surface: The first bit of icing goes on the last part of a cake's decoration.
explanation.definitionFit: A finial is an ornamental knob or spike topping a roof, gable or post.

clue.text: Artist put in the box Irish cross

indicators.note: put in means the artist goes inside the television

parts.note: the box is British slang for television, TV
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist
Erse is the Gaelic language of Ireland

explanation.surface: A painter appears on TV, an angry Irishman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross' looks like angry, but it is the verb meaning to travel across.
explanation.definitionFit: To traverse an area is to travel across it.

clue.text: Money paid for capturing knight and member of royal family

indicators.note: capturing means the word for money paid holds the chess knight inside

parts.note: the price is the money paid for something
N is the chess notation for knight

explanation.surface: A ransom paid for seizing a knight and a royal.
explanation.definitionFit: A prince is the son or close male relative of a monarch.
